messages:
maria: heads up — CI on main for console-ui started failing npm audit gating after yesterday's dependency refresh. I ran a local audit and got 3 transitive CVEs flagged (set-value, yargs-parser, ssri). snippet below

maria: ```
$ npm audit --json
{
  "actions": [...],
  "vulnerabilities": {
    "set-value": {"severity":"high","via":[{"title":"Prototype pollution","url":"https://cve.mitre.org/.."}]},
    "yargs-parser": {"severity":"moderate","via":[{"title":"Argument injection","url":"https://example.com/.."}]},
    "ssri": {"severity":"moderate","via":[{"title":"Integrity bypass","url":"https://example.com/.."}]}
  }
}
```

kevin: are tests actually failing or just the audit step? we shouldn't block a release for low-risk transitive stuff unless exploit paths exist.

maria: audit step is configured as advisory -> fail in CI for main branch. This was added last quarter to enforce hard gating. This PR bumped several build-tool deps which pulled in set-value.

sec-bot: Created security issue SEC-2026-118 linking the audit output and tagged eng-security, eng-platform.

olga: can we patch with overrides/resolutions and open a small PR? that usually reduces lockfile churn compared to full dependency bumps. downside is we need to ensure override doesn't break nested consumers.

tom: overrides look fine but watch for pnpm lockfile churn — last time we applied resolutions across workspace it caused a cascade of package-lock changes in integrator apps. suggestion: do a focused bump on the direct dep that pulls set-value instead of global resolutions. also we should run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI to catch churn early.

ria: we also need to consider backport to release-v1 branch (customers on older console). is the vulnerable path present in v1? Maria, can you run `npm ls set-value` on v1?

maria: running now, will paste results.

maria: ```
$ npm ls set-value
console-ui@main /repo/console-ui
+-- some-direct-dep@2.1.0
| `-- nested-dep@1.4.3
|   `-- set-value@0.4.3
`-- another-direct@3.0.0
    `-- yargs-parser@15.0.1
```

kevin: looks like set-value is nested under nested-dep which we don't own. remediation options: 1) bump nested-dep to a patched version; 2) apply resolution for set-value; 3) add audit exception with justification and mitigations.

olga: given the exploit complexity for prototype pollution here, I'd vote for option 1 if a patched nested-dep exists. fallback to resolutions if no upstream fix. let's aim for a minimal-change PR.

maria: I opened a draft PR linking SEC-2026-118: https://github.com/redwood/console-ui/pull/3421 - it bumps nested-dep to 1.4.5 which advertises removing the vulnerable set-value. CI is running.

buildkite: Pipeline #5842 started for PR #3421 — steps: install -> build -> test -> audit.

tom: CI note: if audit still fails due to lockfile mismatch, add `npm ci --prefer-offline` step to ensure reproducible installs, and keep `--frozen-lockfile` check. that reduces surprises on merge.

maria: CI passed build/tests but audit step still fails because yargs-parser is coming from another direct dep. I can add a second focused bump for that dep.

ria: for release-v1 backport, we should prepare a patch PR but gate it for the next maintenance window. customers on v1 require minimal churn. Maria — can you confirm risk profile once both bumps are in?

maria: yes — after second bump draft PR created (PR #3423). I included unit test runs and smoke tests. no API changes.

kevin: decision: do the focused bumps in main and backport to v1 (cherry-pick PR). avoid global resolutions for now. schedule: merge main PRs after 24h of monitoring in staging, create backport PRs, and plan for a maintenance deploy next Tue during low traffic. owners: maria (PRs), tom (CI changes), olga (security review), ria (backport + customer comms).

olga: I'll do a quick risk review and mark SEC-2026-118 with severity "maintain" -> "action required" and confirm mitigations.

maria: action items posted in issue. i'll also add an automated audit exception category to our security runbook if we need temporary exceptions in future.

kevin: thanks. please post final merge links and I'll update release notes and the incident tracker if needed. :thumbsup:

maria: will do — pinging when PRs merge. :white_check_mark:
